description: Presents the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of decision-making under uncertainty, dynamic programming, deep Q-networks, policy gradients, and actor-critic methods.
learning_objectives: Formulate sequential decision-making problems as Markov Decision Processes (MDPs).
Solve MDPs using dynamic programming (Policy/Value Iteration) and model-free TD methods.
Implement Deep Q-Networks (DQN) with experience replay and target networks.
Master Policy Gradient methods including Actor-Critic, PPO, TRPO, DDPG, and SAC.
outline: Markov Decision Processes: States, actions, transition probabilities, rewards, return, discount factor, Bellman equations.
Dynamic Programming: Policy evaluation, policy iteration, value iteration, dynamic programming optimality.
Model-Free Learning: Monte Carlo methods, Temporal-Difference learning (TD(0), TD(lambda)), SARSA, Q-Learning.
Deep Q-Learning: Function approximation, Deep Q-Networks (DQN), Double DQN, Dueling DQN, Prioritized Experience Replay.
Policy Gradient Methods: REINFORCE theorem, Actor-Critic methods, Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C/A3C), PPO, TRPO, DDPG, SAC.
Exploration & Advanced RL: Multi-armed bandits (UCB, Thompson sampling), Inverse RL, Hierarchical RL, Multi-Agent RL.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.author: Richard S. Sutton, Andrew G. Barto
